**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." This is its wording.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yaman ibn al-Mughira al-'Anzi narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to half the Qur'an, 'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'Say: O disbelievers' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." Then he said: It is gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughira.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

He also said: 'Uqba ibn Mukarram al-'Ammi al-Basri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to me, Salama ibn Wardan informed me, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, O so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with!?" He said: "Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!" [Marry!] (the repetition is from Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2895.)]

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated these three (hadiths); none other of the authors of the books narrated them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾: that is, it moves from its lowest part. ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: meaning, it casts out what is within it of the dead. This was said by more than one of the early (scholars, al-salaf). This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1], and like His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out and casts forth what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3-4].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earth will throw out the fillets of its liver like pillars of gold and silver. The killer will come and say: 'For this I killed.' The one who severed ties of kinship will come and say: 'For this I severed my kinship.' The thief will come and say: 'For this my hand was cut off.' Then they will leave it, and they will take nothing from it."
[(Sahih Muslim no. 1013.)]

* *

His saying: ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: that is, he will be astonished at its matter after it had been stable, still, and firm, while he was resting upon its back. That is, the state changes, and it becomes moving and agitated, and there has come to it from the command of Allah what was prepared for it of the convulsion from which there is no escape. Then it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, from the first and the last. At that time people will be astonished at its matter, and the earth will be changed into another earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: that is, it will report what the doers did upon its back.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, — and al-Tirmidhi and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said, and the wording is his: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us — he is Ibn al-Mubarak — from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will testify against every male and female servant regarding what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such, on such-and-such a day.' This is its news."
[(Musnad 2/374; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3353; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11693.)]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith.

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'a: al-Harith ibn Yazid — who heard Rabi'a al-Jurashi — narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Guard yourselves from the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who acts upon it, good or evil, except that it will inform (of it)."
[(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 5/65; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1/241: "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and he is weak.")]

* *

His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾: al-Bukhari said: "Awha lahā" and "awha ilayhā," and "waha lahā" and "waha ilayhā," are one and the same. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "awha ilayhā" (He inspired it). The apparent meaning is that this is implied to mean "adhina lahā" (He permitted it).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: He said: Its Lord said to it: "Speak," and it spoke.

Mujahid said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "amarahā" (He commanded it). And al-Qurazi said: He commanded it to split open for them.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾: that is, they will return from the places of reckoning. ﴿In scattered groups﴾: that is, in kinds and categories, between wretched and blessed, those directed to Paradise and those directed to the Fire.

Ibn Jurayj said: They will disperse in groups, and they will not gather again, the last of what is upon them (i.e., the final reckoning).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿ashtatan﴾ means "firaqan" (groups).

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: that is, that they may be made to act and be recompensed for what they did in this world, of good and evil. Therefore He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another it is a shield, and for another it is a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethered it in the cause of Allah and lengthened its tether in a meadow or a garden; whatever it eats within that tether in the meadow or the garden is recorded as good deeds for him. And if it breaks its tether and jumps one or two hills, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded as good deeds for him; that horse is a reward for that man. And a man who tethered it out of self-sufficiency and abstinence, and did not forget Allah's right concerning its necks or its backs, it is a shield for him. And a man who tethered it out of pride, ostentation, and enmity, it is a burden for him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Allah did not reveal anything concerning them except this unique and comprehensive verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾"
[(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4962.)]

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, with the same chain.
[(Sahih Muslim no. 987.)]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Sa'sa'a ibn Mu'awiya — the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq — that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and recited to him: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ He said: "Enough for me! I do not care if I hear anything other than it."
[(Musnad 5/59.)]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise in his Tafsir, from Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from his father, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, narrated to us, and he mentioned it.
[(Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11694.)]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Adi, marfu'an (traced to the Prophet ﷺ): "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date, and even with a good word." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7512.)] And in the Sahih: "Do not belittle anything of good, even if you pour from your bucket into the vessel of one who seeks water, and even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face." [(Sahih Muslim no. 2626, from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him.)] And in the Sahih also: "O women of the believers, let no neighbor belittle (a gift to) her neighbor, even if it is a sheep's trotter." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2566, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.)] That is, its hoof. And in another hadith: "Return the beggar even with a burnt hoof." [(Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5/381, Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. 1667, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 665, from the hadith of Umm Bujayd al-Ansariyya, may Allah be pleased with her. Al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith of Umm Bujayd is hasan sahih.")]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O 'A'isha, shield yourself from the Fire even with half a date, for it fills the place of the hungry as it fills the place of the satisfied." Ahmad alone narrated it.
[(Musnad 6/79.)]

And it is reported from 'A'isha that she gave a grape in charity and said: "How many atoms' weight are in it?"
[(It is in al-Muwatta' 2/997 as a balagh (unchained report) from 'A'isha.)]

Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Muslim narrated to us, I heard 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: 'Awf ibn al-Harith ibn al-Tufayl narrated to me that 'A'isha informed him that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O 'A'isha, beware of belittled sins, for they have a seeker from Allah."

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak, with the same chain.
[(Musnad 6/151; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4243.)]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Khattab al-Hassani narrated to me, al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Simak ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to eat with the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [[In A: "min" (from), which is an error.]] So Abu Bakr raised his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will I be recompensed for an atom's weight of evil that I have done?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, whatever you see in this world of what you dislike, it is by the weights of the atoms of evil, and Allah stores up for you the weights of the atoms of good until you meet Him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/173). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (3418), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain, and he said: "No one narrated it from Ayyub except Simak, and no one from him except al-Haytham. It is unique to him, Ziyadah." I say: al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' is weak.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub said: "In the book of Abu Qilabah, from Abu Idris: that Abu Bakr used to eat with the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/174). It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (7103), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, no. (87), "al-Qit'ah al-Ma'qudah," through Ibn Wahb, with the same chain.]].

He also narrated it from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah: that Abu Bakr, and he mentioned it.

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Hayyi ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he said: When ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was sitting, and he wept when it was revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "This surah makes me weep." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Were it not that you sin and commit wrongs, and Allah forgives you, Allah would create a nation that sins and commits wrongs, and He would forgive them" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/175).]].

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah and 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn [Muhammad ibn] al-Mughirah, known as Allan al-Misri, narrated to us, both saying: 'Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: When ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ was revealed, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will I see my deeds?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Those are the great ones, the great ones?" He said: "Yes." I said: "The small ones, the small ones?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Woe to my mother!" He said: "Rejoice, O Abu Sa'id; for a good deed is rewarded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and Allah multiplies it for whom He wills, and an evil deed is recompensed with its like, or Allah forgives it, and none of you will be saved by his deed." I said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" [[In A: "O Prophet of Allah."]] He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/594) and attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim; its final part has a witness in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Abu Zur'ah said: No one narrated this except Ibn Lahi'ah.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. This was because when the verse ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [al-Insan: 8] was revealed, the Muslims thought they would not be rewarded for the little they gave. A needy person would come to their doors, and they would consider it too little to give him a date, a morsel, a nut, or the like, so they would turn him away and say: "This is nothing. We are only rewarded for what we give and love." Others thought they would not be blamed for minor sins: a lie, a glance, backbiting, and the like, saying: "Allah only threatened the Fire for major sins." So He encouraged them to do even a little good, for it will soon grow, and warned them against a little evil, for it will soon grow. Then it was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, meaning the weight of the smallest ant, ﴿of good will see it﴾, meaning in his record, and it will delight him. He said: It is written for every righteous and wicked person: for every evil deed one evil, and for every good deed ten good deeds. Then on the Day of Resurrection Allah will multiply the good deeds of the believers too, tenfold each, and He will erase for him ten evil deeds for each good deed. So whoever's good deeds exceed his evil deeds by an atom's weight enters Paradise.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Rabbih, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of trivial sins, for they gather upon a man until they destroy him." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck an example for them: like a people who alighted in a barren land, and the time for their meal came. A man went and brought a stick, and another man brought a stick, until they gathered a heap, kindled a fire, and cooked what they had thrown into it [[Al-Musnad (1/402).]].

[End of the commentary on Surah "Idha Zulzilat"] [[Added from M, A.]] [And to Allah belongs all praise and grace] [[Added from A.]]

[(Sahih Muslim no. 987.)]

**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." This is its wording.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yaman ibn al-Mughira al-'Anzi narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to half the Qur'an, 'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'Say: O disbelievers' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." Then he said: It is gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughira.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

He also said: 'Uqba ibn Mukarram al-'Ammi al-Basri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to me, Salama ibn Wardan informed me, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, O so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with!?" He said: "Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!" [Marry!] (the repetition is from Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2895.)]

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated these three (hadiths); none other of the authors of the books narrated them.

Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Muslim narrated to us, I heard 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: 'Awf ibn al-Harith ibn al-Tufayl narrated to me that 'A'isha informed him that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O 'A'isha, beware of belittled sins, for they have a seeker from Allah."

**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." This is its wording.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yaman ibn al-Mughira al-'Anzi narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to half the Qur'an, 'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'Say: O disbelievers' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." Then he said: It is gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughira.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

He also said: 'Uqba ibn Mukarram al-'Ammi al-Basri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to me, Salama ibn Wardan informed me, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, O so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with!?" He said: "Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!" [Marry!] (the repetition is from Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2895.)]

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated these three (hadiths); none other of the authors of the books narrated them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾: that is, it moves from its lowest part. ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: meaning, it casts out what is within it of the dead. This was said by more than one of the early (scholars, al-salaf). This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1], and like His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out and casts forth what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3-4].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earth will throw out the fillets of its liver like pillars of gold and silver. The killer will come and say: 'For this I killed.' The one who severed ties of kinship will come and say: 'For this I severed my kinship.' The thief will come and say: 'For this my hand was cut off.' Then they will leave it, and they will take nothing from it."
[(Sahih Muslim no. 1013.)]

* *

His saying: ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: that is, he will be astonished at its matter after it had been stable, still, and firm, while he was resting upon its back. That is, the state changes, and it becomes moving and agitated, and there has come to it from the command of Allah what was prepared for it of the convulsion from which there is no escape. Then it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, from the first and the last. At that time people will be astonished at its matter, and the earth will be changed into another earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: that is, it will report what the doers did upon its back.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, — and al-Tirmidhi and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said, and the wording is his: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us — he is Ibn al-Mubarak — from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will testify against every male and female servant regarding what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such, on such-and-such a day.' This is its news."
[(Musnad 2/374; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3353; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11693.)]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith.

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'a: al-Harith ibn Yazid — who heard Rabi'a al-Jurashi — narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Guard yourselves from the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who acts upon it, good or evil, except that it will inform (of it)."
[(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 5/65; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1/241: "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and he is weak.")]

* *

His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾: al-Bukhari said: "Awha lahā" and "awha ilayhā," and "waha lahā" and "waha ilayhā," are one and the same. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "awha ilayhā" (He inspired it). The apparent meaning is that this is implied to mean "adhina lahā" (He permitted it).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: He said: Its Lord said to it: "Speak," and it spoke.

Mujahid said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "amarahā" (He commanded it). And al-Qurazi said: He commanded it to split open for them.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾: that is, they will return from the places of reckoning. ﴿In scattered groups﴾: that is, in kinds and categories, between wretched and blessed, those directed to Paradise and those directed to the Fire.

Ibn Jurayj said: They will disperse in groups, and they will not gather again, the last of what is upon them (i.e., the final reckoning).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿ashtatan﴾ means "firaqan" (groups).

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: that is, that they may be made to act and be recompensed for what they did in this world, of good and evil. Therefore He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another it is a shield, and for another it is a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethered it in the cause of Allah and lengthened its tether in a meadow or a garden; whatever it eats within that tether in the meadow or the garden is recorded as good deeds for him. And if it breaks its tether and jumps one or two hills, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded as good deeds for him; that horse is a reward for that man. And a man who tethered it out of self-sufficiency and abstinence, and did not forget Allah's right concerning its necks or its backs, it is a shield for him. And a man who tethered it out of pride, ostentation, and enmity, it is a burden for him." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4962.)]

**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." This is its wording.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yaman ibn al-Mughira al-'Anzi narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to half the Qur'an, 'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'Say: O disbelievers' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." Then he said: It is gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughira.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

He also said: 'Uqba ibn Mukarram al-'Ammi al-Basri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to me, Salama ibn Wardan informed me, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, O so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with!?" He said: "Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!" [Marry!] (the repetition is from Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2895.)]

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated these three (hadiths); none other of the authors of the books narrated them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾: that is, it moves from its lowest part. ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: meaning, it casts out what is within it of the dead. This was said by more than one of the early (scholars, al-salaf). This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1], and like His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out and casts forth what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3-4].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earth will throw out the fillets of its liver like pillars of gold and silver. The killer will come and say: 'For this I killed.' The one who severed ties of kinship will come and say: 'For this I severed my kinship.' The thief will come and say: 'For this my hand was cut off.' Then they will leave it, and they will take nothing from it."
[(Sahih Muslim no. 1013.)]

* *

His saying: ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: that is, he will be astonished at its matter after it had been stable, still, and firm, while he was resting upon its back. That is, the state changes, and it becomes moving and agitated, and there has come to it from the command of Allah what was prepared for it of the convulsion from which there is no escape. Then it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, from the first and the last. At that time people will be astonished at its matter, and the earth will be changed into another earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: that is, it will report what the doers did upon its back.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, — and al-Tirmidhi and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said, and the wording is his: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us — he is Ibn al-Mubarak — from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will testify against every male and female servant regarding what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such, on such-and-such a day.' This is its news."
[(Musnad 2/374; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3353; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11693.)]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith.

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'a: al-Harith ibn Yazid — who heard Rabi'a al-Jurashi — narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Guard yourselves from the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who acts upon it, good or evil, except that it will inform (of it)."
[(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 5/65; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1/241: "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and he is weak.")]

* *

His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾: al-Bukhari said: "Awha lahā" and "awha ilayhā," and "waha lahā" and "waha ilayhā," are one and the same. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "awha ilayhā" (He inspired it). The apparent meaning is that this is implied to mean "adhina lahā" (He permitted it).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: He said: Its Lord said to it: "Speak," and it spoke.

Mujahid said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "amarahā" (He commanded it). And al-Qurazi said: He commanded it to split open for them.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾: that is, they will return from the places of reckoning. ﴿In scattered groups﴾: that is, in kinds and categories, between wretched and blessed, those directed to Paradise and those directed to the Fire.

Ibn Jurayj said: They will disperse in groups, and they will not gather again, the last of what is upon them (i.e., the final reckoning).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿ashtatan﴾ means "firaqan" (groups).

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: that is, that they may be made to act and be recompensed for what they did in this world, of good and evil. Therefore He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another it is a shield, and for another it is a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethered it in the cause of Allah and lengthened its tether in a meadow or a garden; whatever it eats within that tether in the meadow or the garden is recorded as good deeds for him. And if it breaks its tether and jumps one or two hills, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded as good deeds for him; that horse is a reward for that man. And a man who tethered it out of self-sufficiency and abstinence, and did not forget Allah's right concerning its necks or its backs, it is a shield for him. And a man who tethered it out of pride, ostentation, and enmity, it is a burden for him." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Allah did not reveal anything concerning them except this unique and comprehensive verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾"
[(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4962.)]

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, with the same chain.
[(Sahih Muslim no. 987.)]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Sa'sa'a ibn Mu'awiya — the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq — that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and recited to him: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ He said: "Enough for me! I do not care if I hear anything other than it."
[(Musnad 5/59.)]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise in his Tafsir, from Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from his father, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, narrated to us, and he mentioned it.
[(Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11694.)]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Adi, marfu'an (traced to the Prophet ﷺ): "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date, and even with a good word." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7512.)] And in the Sahih: "Do not belittle anything of good, even if you pour from your bucket into the vessel of one who seeks water, and even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face." [(Sahih Muslim no. 2626, from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him.)] And in the Sahih also: "O women of the believers, let no neighbor belittle (a gift to) her neighbor, even if it is a sheep's trotter." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2566, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.)] That is, its hoof. And in another hadith: "Return the beggar even with a burnt hoof." [(Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5/381, Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. 1667, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 665, from the hadith of Umm Bujayd al-Ansariyya, may Allah be pleased with her. Al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith of Umm Bujayd is hasan sahih.")]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O 'A'isha, shield yourself from the Fire even with half a date, for it fills the place of the hungry as it fills the place of the satisfied." Ahmad alone narrated it.
[(Musnad 6/79.)]

And it is reported from 'A'isha that she gave a grape in charity and said: "How many atoms' weight are in it?"
[(It is in al-Muwatta' 2/997 as a balagh (unchained report) from 'A'isha.)]

Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Muslim narrated to us, I heard 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: 'Awf ibn al-Harith ibn al-Tufayl narrated to me that 'A'isha informed him that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O 'A'isha, beware of belittled sins, for they have a seeker from Allah."

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak, with the same chain.
[(Musnad 6/151; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4243.)]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Khattab al-Hassani narrated to me, al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Simak ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to eat with the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [[In A: "min" (from), which is an error.]] So Abu Bakr raised his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will I be recompensed for an atom's weight of evil that I have done?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, whatever you see in this world of what you dislike, it is by the weights of the atoms of evil, and Allah stores up for you the weights of the atoms of good until you meet Him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/173). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (3418), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain, and he said: "No one narrated it from Ayyub except Simak, and no one from him except al-Haytham. It is unique to him, Ziyadah." I say: al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' is weak.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub said: "In the book of Abu Qilabah, from Abu Idris: that Abu Bakr used to eat with the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/174). It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (7103), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, no. (87), "al-Qit'ah al-Ma'qudah," through Ibn Wahb, with the same chain.]].

He also narrated it from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah: that Abu Bakr, and he mentioned it.

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Hayyi ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he said: When ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was sitting, and he wept when it was revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "This surah makes me weep." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Were it not that you sin and commit wrongs, and Allah forgives you, Allah would create a nation that sins and commits wrongs, and He would forgive them" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/175).]].

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah and 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn [Muhammad ibn] al-Mughirah, known as Allan al-Misri, narrated to us, both saying: 'Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: When ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ was revealed, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will I see my deeds?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Those are the great ones, the great ones?" He said: "Yes." I said: "The small ones, the small ones?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Woe to my mother!" He said: "Rejoice, O Abu Sa'id; for a good deed is rewarded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and Allah multiplies it for whom He wills, and an evil deed is recompensed with its like, or Allah forgives it, and none of you will be saved by his deed." I said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" [[In A: "O Prophet of Allah."]] He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/594) and attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim; its final part has a witness in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Abu Zur'ah said: No one narrated this except Ibn Lahi'ah.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. This was because when the verse ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [al-Insan: 8] was revealed, the Muslims thought they would not be rewarded for the little they gave. A needy person would come to their doors, and they would consider it too little to give him a date, a morsel, a nut, or the like, so they would turn him away and say: "This is nothing. We are only rewarded for what we give and love." Others thought they would not be blamed for minor sins: a lie, a glance, backbiting, and the like, saying: "Allah only threatened the Fire for major sins." So He encouraged them to do even a little good, for it will soon grow, and warned them against a little evil, for it will soon grow. Then it was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, meaning the weight of the smallest ant, ﴿of good will see it﴾, meaning in his record, and it will delight him. He said: It is written for every righteous and wicked person: for every evil deed one evil, and for every good deed ten good deeds. Then on the Day of Resurrection Allah will multiply the good deeds of the believers too, tenfold each, and He will erase for him ten evil deeds for each good deed. So whoever's good deeds exceed his evil deeds by an atom's weight enters Paradise.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Rabbih, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of trivial sins, for they gather upon a man until they destroy him." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck an example for them: like a people who alighted in a barren land, and the time for their meal came. A man went and brought a stick, and another man brought a stick, until they gathered a heap, kindled a fire, and cooked what they had thrown into it [[Al-Musnad (1/402).]].

**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." [(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise in his Tafsir, from Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from his father, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, narrated to us, and he mentioned it.
[(Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11694.)]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Adi, marfu'an (traced to the Prophet ﷺ): "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date, and even with a good word." [(Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7512.)] And in the Sahih: "Do not belittle anything of good, even if you pour from your bucket into the vessel of one who seeks water, and even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face." [(Sahih Muslim no. 2626, from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him.)] And in the Sahih also: "O women of the believers, let no neighbor belittle (a gift to) her neighbor, even if it is a sheep's trotter." [(Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5/381, Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. 1667, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 665, from the hadith of Umm Bujayd al-Ansariyya, may Allah be pleased with her. Al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith of Umm Bujayd is hasan sahih.")]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O 'A'isha, shield yourself from the Fire even with half a date, for it fills the place of the hungry as it fills the place of the satisfied." [(Musnad 6/79.)]

[(It is in al-Muwatta' 2/997 as a balagh (unchained report) from 'A'isha.)]

[(Musnad 6/151; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4243.)]

He said: "O Abu Bakr, whatever you see in this world of what you dislike, it is by the weights of the atoms of evil, and Allah stores up for you the weights of the atoms of good until you meet Him on the Day of Resurrection." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/173). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (3418), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain, and he said: "No one narrated it from Ayyub except Simak, and no one from him except al-Haytham. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu al-Khattab, with the same chain. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub said: "In the book of Abu Qilabah, from Abu Idris: that Abu Bakr used to eat with the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/174). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "This surah makes me weep." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Were it not that you sin and commit wrongs, and Allah forgives you, Allah would create a nation that sins and commits wrongs, and He would forgive them" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/175).]].

**Commentary on Surah Al-Zalzalah (Surah 99)**

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah "When the Earth Is Shaken" (Idha Zulzilat)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sada'i, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Teach me (aqri'ni), O Messenger of Allah." He said to him: "Recite three (surahs) from Dhawat al-Ra." The man said to him: "My age has grown great, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick." He said: "Then recite from Dhawat Ha Mim." He said the same thing as his first statement. He said: "Recite three of the Musabbihat." He said the same thing. The man said: "But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah." So he taught him: "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking" until he finished it. The man said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it." Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The man has prospered! The man has prospered!" Then he said: "Bring him to me." He came, and he said to him: "I have been commanded (concerning) the Day of Sacrifice; Allah has made it a festival for this Ummah." The man said to him: "What if I do not find anything except a female loaned animal that I sacrifice?" He said: "No. Rather, you take from your hair, trim your nails, trim your moustache, and shave your pubic hair. That is the completion of your sacrifice before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with the same chain.
[(Musnad 2/169; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1399; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/212.)]

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi al-Basri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Salm ibn Salih al-'Ijli narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites 'When (the earth) is shaken' is given the reward of half the Qur'an." Then he said: This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Salm.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2893.)]

Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi, from al-Hasan ibn Salm, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." This is its wording.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Yaman ibn al-Mughira al-'Anzi narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'When (the earth) is shaken' is equal to half the Qur'an, 'Say: He is Allah, the One' is equal to a third of the Qur'an, and 'Say: O disbelievers' is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an." Then he said: It is gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughira.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2894.)]

He also said: 'Uqba ibn Mukarram al-'Ammi al-Basri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to me, Salama ibn Wardan informed me, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, O so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with!?" He said: "Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!" [Marry!] (the repetition is from Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
[(Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2895.)]

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated these three (hadiths); none other of the authors of the books narrated them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾: that is, it moves from its lowest part. ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: meaning, it casts out what is within it of the dead. This was said by more than one of the early (scholars, al-salaf). This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1], and like His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out and casts forth what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3-4].

Muslim said in his Sahih: Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earth will throw out the fillets of its liver like pillars of gold and silver. The killer will come and say: 'For this I killed.' The one who severed ties of kinship will come and say: 'For this I severed my kinship.' The thief will come and say: 'For this my hand was cut off.' Then they will leave it, and they will take nothing from it."
[(Sahih Muslim no. 1013.)]

* *

His saying: ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: that is, he will be astonished at its matter after it had been stable, still, and firm, while he was resting upon its back. That is, the state changes, and it becomes moving and agitated, and there has come to it from the command of Allah what was prepared for it of the convulsion from which there is no escape. Then it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, from the first and the last. At that time people will be astonished at its matter, and the earth will be changed into another earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: that is, it will report what the doers did upon its back.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, — and al-Tirmidhi and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said, and the wording is his: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us — he is Ibn al-Mubarak — from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will testify against every male and female servant regarding what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such, on such-and-such a day.' This is its news."
[(Musnad 2/374; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3353; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11693.)]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith.

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'a: al-Harith ibn Yazid — who heard Rabi'a al-Jurashi — narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Guard yourselves from the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who acts upon it, good or evil, except that it will inform (of it)."
[(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 5/65; al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1/241: "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and he is weak.")]

His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾: al-Bukhari said: "Awha lahā" and "awha ilayhā," and "waha lahā" and "waha ilayhā," are one and the same. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "awha ilayhā" (He inspired it). The apparent meaning is that this is implied to mean "adhina lahā" (He permitted it).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾: He said: Its Lord said to it: "Speak," and it spoke.

Mujahid said: ﴿awha lahā﴾ means "amarahā" (He commanded it). And al-Qurazi said: He commanded it to split open for them.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾: that is, they will return from the places of reckoning. ﴿In scattered groups﴾: that is, in kinds and categories, between wretched and blessed, those directed to Paradise and those directed to the Fire.

Ibn Jurayj said: They will disperse in groups, and they will not gather again, the last of what is upon them (i.e., the final reckoning).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿ashtatan﴾ means "firaqan" (groups).

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: that is, that they may be made to act and be recompensed for what they did in this world, of good and evil. Therefore He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another it is a shield, and for another it is a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethered it in the cause of Allah and lengthened its tether in a meadow or a garden; whatever it eats within that tether in the meadow or the garden is recorded as good deeds for him. And if it breaks its tether and jumps one or two hills, its traces and its dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded as good deeds for him; that horse is a reward for that man. And a man who tethered it out of self-sufficiency and abstinence, and did not forget Allah's right concerning its necks or its backs, it is a shield for him. And a man who tethered it out of pride, ostentation, and enmity, it is a burden for him." He said: "Rejoice, O Abu Sa'id; for a good deed is rewarded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and Allah multiplies it for whom He wills, and an evil deed is recompensed with its like, or Allah forgives it, and none of you will be saved by his deed." I said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" [[In A: "O Prophet of Allah."]] He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/594) and attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim; its final part has a witness in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Abu Zur'ah said: No one narrated this except Ibn Lahi'ah.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. This was because when the verse ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [al-Insan: 8] was revealed, the Muslims thought they would not be rewarded for the little they gave. A needy person would come to their doors, and they would consider it too little to give him a date, a morsel, a nut, or the like, so they would turn him away and say: "This is nothing. We are only rewarded for what we give and love." Others thought they would not be blamed for minor sins: a lie, a glance, backbiting, and the like, saying: "Allah only threatened the Fire for major sins." So He encouraged them to do even a little good, for it will soon grow, and warned them against a little evil, for it will soon grow. Then it was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, meaning the weight of the smallest ant, ﴿of good will see it﴾, meaning in his record, and it will delight him. He said: It is written for every righteous and wicked person: for every evil deed one evil, and for every good deed ten good deeds. Then on the Day of Resurrection Allah will multiply the good deeds of the believers too, tenfold each, and He will erase for him ten evil deeds for each good deed. So whoever's good deeds exceed his evil deeds by an atom's weight enters Paradise.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Rabbih, from Abu 'Iyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of trivial sins, for they gather upon a man until they destroy him." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck an example for them: like a people who alighted in a barren land, and the time for their meal came. A man went and brought a stick, and another man brought a stick, until they gathered a heap, kindled a fire, and cooked what they had thrown into it [[Al-Musnad (1/402).]].
